finding: GameInfo.LastCustomIdOwner is the DDV Player/User ID represented as the mdc value in existing DDV Profile Converter/Wand backup naming and is suitable as the stable DDV Profile identity source for the current v1.25 contract.

requirements: Identifier remains stable across ordinary save/resave of the same DDV Profile.
Identifier semantics are defined for Nintendo Switch and Steam/Windows v1.25.0 and for the same cloud-linked profile observed across platforms.
Identifier is independent of Moonstones, receipts, Premium/DLC entitlements, online auth tokens and platform credentials.
Identifier can be extracted locally without uploading or persistently storing the entire raw save.
Core documents clone/copy/reset/new-profile behavior and collision/domain semantics.
Core documents privacy/linkability characteristics and the exact field/source provenance.
evidenceExpected: Controlled same-profile before/after normal save/resave comparison.
Negative comparison against a distinct DDV Profile.

evidence: Existing Wand/Converter backup contract uses mdc{GameInfo.LastCustomIdOwner}.

Nintendo Switch v1.25.0 schema-624 accepted baseline and a later fresh synced Steam/Windows v1.25.0 schema-624 baseline for the same cloud-linked DDV Profile contain exactly the same GameInfo.LastCustomIdOwner value.
The canonical stored Steam decrypted filename's mdc component exactly matches GameInfo.LastCustomIdOwner.
Owner reports this same value is the in-game User ID used for official support identification.
Gameloft DDV Help Center documents the in-game Player ID path as Settings -> Help -> Show User ID.
remainingUnknowns: Global uniqueness/collision behavior is not independently documented in the official help article; backend uniqueness must fail closed on digest collision.

Reset/new-profile lifecycle semantics should be documented when a controlled reset/new-profile fixture becomes available, but this does not block using the official Player ID as the current Linked DDV Profile identity source.
